title: A Change branch is known by its name, and the Fix path gets a prefix of its own
context: The trailer rule applies to Change commits only: a Fix-path commit must omit `Blueprint-Change`. So a commit-msg check has to know whether the commit belongs to a Change, and the commit message alone cannot tell it — a Change commit that forgot its trailer looks exactly like a Fix-path commit. The Change's own directory under `blueprint/content/changes/` is gitignored, so it is absent in a fresh worktree and in CI, and a check keyed on it would disagree between hook and CI. The branch name is the remaining signal, but `WORKFLOW.md` binds Change branches to `feat/<slug>`, `fix/<slug>` or `refactor/<slug>` and gives the Fix path no name of its own. Of the branches merged into `dev` since the first `Blueprint-Change` trailer on 2026-08-11, nine `fix/` and four `refactor/` branches carried no trailer, beside eight `fix/` and three `feat/` branches that were Changes, so the prefix does not identify a Change today.
decision: A branch named `feat/<slug>`, `fix/<slug>` or `refactor/<slug>` is a Change branch, and every commit on it carries `Blueprint-Change: <slug>` with the same slug as the branch name. Fix-path work uses `hotfix/<slug>` whatever its commit type, including docs, config and refactors. Any other branch — `dev`, `hotfix/*`, `chore/*`, `docs/*`, an agent's `claude/*` worktree branch — has no trailer requirement. Outside `hotfix/*`, where the Fix path forbids it, a trailer is still allowed, as on the `docs/` follow-up branch that recorded work for an already-merged Change. The commit-msg hook reads the current branch name; when it cannot, as in a detached HEAD during a rebase, it skips the rule. CI reads the pull request's head branch name and applies the same rule to every commit in the range, so CI remains the authority.

alternatives.option: Treat a branch as a Change branch when `blueprint/content/changes/<slug>/` exists
alternatives.reason: The directory is gitignored. It is missing in a fresh worktree and in CI, so the hook and CI would reach opposite verdicts on the same commit.

alternatives.option: Check the message alone: require `Blueprint-Change` whenever `Implements` or `Migration` is present
alternatives.reason: It misses a Change commit that carries no trailer at all, which is the failure that forced the rebase rewrite during two-gate-workflow.

alternatives.option: Keep the current prefixes and give Change branches a distinct one instead, such as `change/<slug>`
alternatives.reason: A Change pushed to a habitual `feat/` branch would silently skip the check in both hook and CI. With the Fix path moved, the habitual mistake — Fix-path work on `fix/` — is rejected loudly at the first commit.

consequences: The value of the trailer is checked, not only its presence, so a mistyped slug is rejected; commitlint's `trailer-exists` cannot do this, so the check lives in the one local plugin.
Fix-path work on a `fix/` or `refactor/` branch out of habit is rejected at its first commit, which is the intended way the new prefix is learned.
A Change commit made on an arbitrarily named branch, such as an agent worktree, passes the hook and is caught by CI once the commits reach the Change branch's pull request.
revisitTriggers: Change branches start being created under a name that does not carry the slug.
The Fix path is merged into the Change path or removed.
